title: Applied Chemistry
semester_basis: CSE semester grid
mode_basis: BTech is a fully residential programme (UG Manual 2.4.1)

title: Environmental Science
semester_basis: CSE semester grid
mode_basis: BTech is a fully residential programme (UG Manual 2.4.1)
syllabus: Understanding our environment: atmosphere composition and behaviour, temperature and pressure profile of atmosphere, Atmospheric Photochemistry: Electromagnetic radiations, kinetics of thermal and photochemical processes, Reactions in the upper atmosphere, photo processes in the troposphere, photochemical smog, photosynthesis, Ozone chemistry, brief overviews of ozone depletion and atmospheric pollutants. Organic and Inorganic chemicals in environment: Ecosystem, flow of energy and nutrient cycles, sustainability, toxicity, polychlorinated hydrocarbons like DDT, polymers, detergents. impact on environment.

title: Data Structures

mode_basis: BTech is a fully residential programme (UG Manual 2.4.1)

Input/Output Organization: I/O Subblock – I/O techniques – interrupts – polling – DMA; Pipelining: Instructions pipeline, hazards.

title: Compiler Design

mode_basis: BTech is a fully residential programme (UG Manual 2.4.1)
syllabus: Compiler structure: analysis-synthesis model of compilation – various phases of a compiler – tool based approach to compiler construction; Phases of compiler design: Lexical analysis; syntax analysis; syntax-directed translation; type checking; run time system; intermediate code generation; machine- independent optimizations; code generation.

title: Database Management Systems
semester_basis: CSE semester grid

title: Artificial Intelligence
semester_basis: CSE semester grid

title: AI-Augmented Software Development
semester_basis: CSE semester grid
mode_basis: BTech is a fully residential programme (UG Manual 2.4.1)
syllabus: Introduction to LLM-based software engineering: Role of LLMs in the software development lifecycle – coding assistants – testing and debugging support – documentation and review – limitations of LLM outputs – academic integrity and responsible use. Prompting as interface design: Role and task specification – constraints and acceptance criteria – input/output formatting – structured prompting – prompt refinement for software tasks – prompt reuse as configuration artifact. LLMs as software components: LLM APIs – request/response patterns – context handling – conversation state – output parsing – schema-based validation – error handling and retries. Structured outputs and integration: JSON outputs – lightweight schemas – deterministic wrappers – validation before execution – integration into software pipelines. From assistants to agents: Chatbots versus agents – perceive-think- act-observe loop – tool use – simple state handling – single-agent task execution. Tools and tool registries: Function/tool calling – tool abstraction – file, search, and execution tools – schemas for tools – permissions and scope control. Agent harness engineering: Harness definition – bounded execution – step limits – runtime policies – trace logging – human-in-the-loop approvals – failure handling and recovery. Agentic workflow patterns: ReAct-style loops – planner-executor pattern – retrieval-assisted workflows – choosing the simplest effective orchestration pattern. Evaluation harnesses: Task suites – success criteria – regression testing – step count, latency, and error metrics – qualitative evaluation – LLM-as-judge and rubric-based assessment. Observability and debugging: Trajectories and traces – prompt/tool/output inspection – episode logging – failure attribution – improving prompts, tools, and harness settings from evidence. Safety and governance: Prompt injection overview – unsafe tool use – privacy and data leakage risks – permission design – sandboxing – human review for high-impact actions. Capstone development and review: Team project planning – design of an LLM-integrated or agentic system – implementation with runtime harness and evaluation harness – demo and technical reflection.
